label: Email 1 · Monday 12 October · from Vishen
to: Expert & Authority community first (summit registrants and Mastery students), then the Members list once Vishen has approved his lines
purpose: Thank the community, announce the AI for Founders Summit, say the survey is coming, introduce the person reading the answers. Co-creation, not marketing.
subjects: You built Expert & Authority with us. Here's what's next.
A thank-you, and a new summit
Help us build AI for Founders
We're opening the curriculum before we finish it
preview: Expert & Authority sold out. Thank you. Now I want your help with the next one.
cta: Save my seat at the AI for Founders Summit
body:
Hi [Name],

Expert & Authority Mastery sold out.

I want to say thank you before anything else. You came to the summit, you asked hard questions in the Q&A, you told us what you were building and what was in the way. The programme that's running right now was shaped by that. The curriculum came out of your survey answers before a single lesson was written. That's the only way I know how to build.

So here's what's next.

On 30 October to 1 November we're running a new, free, three-day event: the **AI for Founders Summit**.

It's not about learning AI. We already have a programme for that. This one is about the business. Specifically, the founder's problem nobody teaches: everything still runs through you. Every lead, every proposal, every client question, every decision waits for your hours. You built the business to be free and somewhere along the way it took the freedom. [Vishen: your own Mindvalley example here, two sentences, the one from the story interview.]

Over three days we'll show you what to automate first in your business, then build it live, step by step. The company brain. The lead that never goes cold. Content in your own voice.

Here's where you come in.

Back in 2015 we built a programme with our community instead of for it. We shared the rough outline, asked what was missing, and published the version they'd shaped. It was the best launch we'd ever done, and the programme was better for it.

I want to do that again. This week you'll get a short survey from us: where your business is, what eats your week, what you'd want a programme like this to fix first. Then we'll publish the curriculum for the summit and the Mastery, openly, before it's finished, and ask you what's missing.

[Photo: Vishen and Gareth, MVU or the KL office. Working, not posed. Group shot with Jaideep if one exists.]

The person reading your answers is Gareth Winter, our Head of Content and Creative Director. Gareth designs our curricula. He'll take what you tell us and publish version two of the programme with your input in it, so you can see exactly what changed because of you.

Save your seat here, and watch for the survey.

**[Save my seat at the AI for Founders Summit]**

Vishen

P.S. from Gareth: I read every answer, not a summary of them. The questions you asked in the Expert & Authority survey are already in this curriculum. Tell me what's missing, and you'll see it in the next version. Gareth
notes: About 380 words, inside the event-invite band. One primary call to action.
Optional question handoff after everything still runs through you: How many of this week's decisions could only you have made?
Role credit for consistent use everywhere: Gareth Winter, Head of Content and Creative Director, designs Mindvalley's curricula.
Register: no exclamation marks, no formal connectives, no triple repetition, one coined idea (co-create) used three times, the enemy is the inherited setup of the business and never the reader.
Images: Gareth is attaching options separately for marketing to choose from.

label: Email 2 · later the same week · from Gareth
to: Everyone who received email 1, two to three days later. Carries the outline link and the survey link.
purpose: Deliver the survey Vishen promised, with the outline alongside it, and make the ask feel like partnership rather than market research.
subjects: The AI for Founders curriculum, before it's finished
Eight modules. Tell us what's missing.
Vishen said a survey was coming. Here it is.
preview: Eight modules, sixteen weeks, nothing fixed yet. Eight minutes of your time shapes version two.
body:
Hi [Name],

Vishen said a survey was coming. Here it is, and here is what it is for.

We have drafted the AI for Founders Mastery: eight modules, one for each part of a business that still runs through its founder. Strategy, the company brain, marketing, sales, operations, team, finance, and what to build next. Each has a lesson and a lab. You can read the outline here: [outline link].

It is a draft on purpose. Before we decide who teaches each lesson, we want to know whether we are teaching the right things. So the survey asks about your business first: where your hours go, what you have tried with AI, what stopped you, and what would make sixteen weeks worth it. Then it asks you to go through the outline and tell us what is missing, where to go deeper, and what to skip. About eight minutes.

I read every answer. On [date] we publish version two with the changes marked, so you can see what moved because of you.

**[Take the survey]**

Gareth Winter
Head of Content and Creative Director, Mindvalley

P.S. The last question asks whether you would review version two before anyone else sees it, or test one of the systems in your own business. That is the founding circle. It is small, and it is open now.
notes: About 230 words. Two links, one button. The outline link goes to the Curriculum Outline page; the survey link carries the recipient's email so the contact question is pre-filled.
Reminder on Friday to non-openers and partial completions only: subject Still open: the AI for Founders survey, body three lines, same button.
Signed by Gareth because email 1 introduced him as the person reading the answers; the reply address should be one a person reads.
